claims.text: In sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, the surface-energy term dominates configurational entropy.
Bulk high-entropy alloys typically exhibit sluggish diffusion.
Elevated temperature activates rapid surface diffusion according to an Arrhenius dependence.
Au and Cu have lower surface energies than Co, Ni, and Pt.
Au and Cu have higher vapor pressures than Co, Ni, and Pt under the proposed heating conditions.
Free-energy minimization causes Au and Cu to segregate to the nanoparticle surface.
Surface segregation produces an outward atomic flux followed by evaporation of Au and Cu.
Evaporation and mass transfer cause nanoparticle shrinkage and broadening of the size distribution through Ostwald ripening.
The elliptical-to-spherical shape transition is caused by surface-tension minimization overcoming bulk-lattice kinetic barriers.
PLD-grown sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles likely contain a high density of defects and nonequilibrium surface states.
The pure-element surface energies are approximately 1.25 J/m² for Au, 1.79 J/m² for Cu, and 2.5 J/m² for Pt.
Higher curvature raises the chemical potential of smaller nanoparticles and drives material from small particles to large particles.
Fast surface diffusion bypasses bulk sluggish diffusion and is less sensitive to HEA lattice mismatch.
The critical temperature for rapid Au/Cu segregation and evaporation is between 700 K and 850 K.
Particles smaller than 5 nm will disappear before larger particles.
After heating, surviving nanoparticles will be enriched in Pt, Co, and Ni and depleted in Au and Cu.
Configurational entropy can stabilize an FCC phase in bulk high-entropy alloys.
Sluggish diffusion prevents segregation and evaporation up to the melting point.
The proposed surface-energy-dominated mechanism is valid only for particles smaller than 10 nm.
For particles larger than 50 nm, entropy stabilization and bulk sluggish diffusion will prevent significant segregation and evaporation over the proposed temperature range.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the bulk-HEA 'sluggish diffusion' process becomes active at elevated temperature, whereas the mechanism says bulk sluggish diffusion is bypassed and surface diffusion is the active transport pathway. The intended distinction between bulk and surface diffusion is not maintained consistently.

The design describes simulations containing both surface-energy gradients and element-specific evaporation rates, but the rule interprets agreement as evidence that surface-energy gradients alone explain the behavior. Agreement would not isolate the surface-energy gradient from the separately parameterized evaporation process.
